up.note: This is the OSSS inequality and the reason \(\mathrm{osss}(f)\) is in the zoo at all. For any decision tree $T$ computing $f$, writing $\delta_i(T) = \Pr_x[T\text{ reads }x_i]$, $$\mathrm{Var}(f)\ \le\ \sum_i \delta_i(T)\,\mathrm{Inf}_i(f)\ \le\ \mathrm{MaxInf}(f)\sum_i\delta_i(T) = \mathrm{MaxInf}(f)\cdot\mathbb{E}_x[\#\text{queries of }T\text{ on }x].$$ So $\mathrm{osss}(f)$ is a lower bound on the expected number of queries, not merely on the depth. A zero-error randomized algorithm is a distribution over such trees, and averaging the inequality over that distribution leaves it intact, so the bound is against $\bar{\mathrm{R}}_0 = \mathrm{R}_0$ and hence against $\mathrm{D}$ by closure. The averaging step is not in [OSSS05], which states the deterministic case.

lo.note: $\mathrm{Var} = \Theta(m^3 2^{-3m})$ against $\mathrm{MaxInf} = 12(m-2)^2 2^{6-3m}$ gives $\mathrm{osss} = \Theta(m)$, and $\mathrm{R}_0(\mathrm{SCORPION}) = \Theta(m)$: the bound is attained, constants aside. \(\mathrm{Tribes}_{w,s}\) attains it to within the $\log$ that KKL forces on any function.

facts: $1\le\mathrm{osss}(f)$, since $\mathrm{MaxInf}\le\mathrm{Var}$ (a single coordinate cannot carry more than all of the variance). Equality for $\oplus_n$ and for a dictator.
$\mathrm{osss}(f) = O(n/\log n)$ by KKL, and \(\mathrm{Tribes}_{w,s}\) attains it: no measure of this shape can ever be within a $\log$ of $n$.
$\mathrm{osss}(f)\le \bar{\mathrm{R}}_0(f) = \mathrm{R}_0(f)\le\mathrm{D}(f)$: OSSS applies to each tree in the support of a Las Vegas algorithm, and averaging preserves the inequality.

It is a weak lower bound and honest about it: $\mathrm{osss}(\oplus_n) = 1$, $\mathrm{osss}(\mathrm{OR}_n) = \Theta(1)$, $\mathrm{osss}(\mathrm{MAJ}_n) = \Theta(\sqrt n)$, all against $\mathrm{D} = n$. It is tight for \(\mathrm{SCORP}_m\) and for \(\mathrm{Tribes}_{w,s}\) up to the $\log$.

The famous corollary of OSSS is for monotone transitive $f$: there $\mathrm{Inf}_i = \hat f(\{i\})$ is the same for every $i$, so $\mathrm{MaxInf} = \mathrm{I}(f)/n \le \Delta(f)/n$ and $\mathrm{Var}\le\Delta(f)^2/n$, giving $\Delta(f) = \Omega(\sqrt{n\,\mathrm{Var}})$ -- a lower bound on average depth from symmetry alone.

up.note:
Pigeonhole on the spectrum. The non-empty Fourier coefficients of $f$ number at most
$\mathrm{spar}(f)$ and carry total weight $\mathrm{Var}(f)$, so some $S\ne\emptyset$ has
$\hat f(S)^2 \ge \mathrm{Var}(f)/\mathrm{spar}(f)$; any $i\in S$ then has
$\mathrm{Inf}_i(f) = \sum_{T\ni i}\hat f(T)^2 \ge \hat f(S)^2$, giving
$\mathrm{MaxInf}\ge\mathrm{Var}/\mathrm{spar}$. Very lossy: the best separation on record
is no separation at all, since every sparse function in the zoo also has
$\mathrm{osss} = O(1)$. A much stronger bound should follow from
$\mathrm{osss}\le\mathrm{D}$ together with the $\mathrm{D}$ versus $\mathrm{spar}$
literature, which the zoo does not yet record as a relation.
